candidates.name: GHD Hip Extension

distinctFrom.why: the GHD holds the hips over a horizontal pad with the knees free to bend, letting the glutes work through a longer hip-extension range with less lower-back involvement than the fixed 45-degree angled bench

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning
candidates.notes: The existing "GHD Sit-Up" row is the same apparatus’s spinal-flexion exercise (per the brief, that one should be never_auto); this hip-extension movement on the same apparatus is a separate hinge-pattern stimulus without that flexion loading, so it is not held to the same tier.

candidates.name: Trap Bar Deadlift (Low Handle)

distinctFrom.why: range/depth class differs (EL-2): the low handles sit closer to the floor, increasing knee and hip flexion at the start and moving the demand closer to a conventional barbell deadlift than the existing row’s (high-handle) shorter pull

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: No dedicated trap-bar coarse equipment value exists in this vocabulary; tagged "barbell", matching the existing "Trap Bar Deadlift" row.

candidates.name: Trap Bar Row

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: the trap bar is only seeded for the deadlift and shrug, never a bent-over row; the neutral-grip handles change the pull path versus a straight bar

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Bent-over row using the trap bar’s neutral handles; a shoulder-friendlier alternative to a pronated-grip barbell row.

candidates.name: Trap Bar Floor Press

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs (trap bar’s neutral handles vs a straight barbell); the neutral grip changes shoulder rotation demand through the same floor-limited ROM

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Lying inside the trap bar’s frame, pressing the neutral handles; a shoulder-friendlier floor press variant.

candidates.name: Cambered Bar Bench Press

distinctFrom.why: this is a horizontal press pattern, not a squat; the two rows share only the implement, not the training stimulus

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: The bend lets the hands drop below the chest, extending stretch ROM at the bottom versus a straight bar; a common accommodating-ROM pressing tool.

candidates.name: Zercher Deadlift

distinctFrom.why: movement pattern differs (hinge, not squat): the bar stays in the crook of the elbows through a hip-hinge pull rather than a knee-and-hip squat descent

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Less common than the Zercher squat; the elbow-crook hold is the shared coaching point, the pattern is not.

candidates.name: Axle Deadlift

distinctFrom.why: grip changes the prime mover/demand (EL-2): the thick (typically 2-inch) axle diameter forces an open, crush-limited grip that a standard-diameter bar at any hand width does not create

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning
candidates.notes: A strongman axle bar rather than a standard barbell diameter; no dedicated coarse equipment value exists for it, so it is tagged "barbell" like the corpus’s other specialty-bar rows.

candidates.name: Log Press

distinctFrom.why: new movement family for this corpus: a strongman log implement, neutral-grip and cylindrical, presses differently from any bar the corpus seeds

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Strongman implement; never_auto per EL-5 ("strongman implement" is one of the five categories the ruling names explicitly). No dedicated coarse equipment value for a log; tagged "barbell" as the closest bucket, same treatment as the other specialty bars.

candidates.name: Swiss Bar Bench Press

distinctFrom.why: grip changes the prime mover/demand (EL-2): the fixed neutral (palms-facing) grip removes the shoulder external-rotation position a pronated-grip press requires, regardless of hand width

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: No dedicated coarse equipment value for a Swiss/football bar; tagged "barbell" as the closest bucket.

candidates.name: Swiss Bar Row

distinctFrom.why: implement family differs at the mechanical level: the Swiss bar’s multiple neutral-grip handle positions let hand width be chosen, where the trap bar’s width is fixed by its frame

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: No dedicated coarse equipment value for a Swiss bar; tagged "barbell".

candidates.name: Chaos Bench Press

distinctFrom.why: plates hang from bands/chains off the bar ends and swing, adding a continuously shifting balance demand a rigid cambered bar does not have

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Setup complexity (bands/chains rigged to each end) and the instability skill it trains keep it niche rather than specialist.

candidates.name: Band-Resisted Bench Press

distinctFrom.why: loading vector differs (EL-2): bands anchored to the rack add resistance that increases through the ROM (more tension at lockout), a different strength curve from a flat plate load

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Accommodating-resistance technique; bands anchored to the rack or floor, not the "Band Chest Press" seeded row (which is band-only, no bar).

candidates.name: Chain-Loaded Bench Press

distinctFrom.why: chains add resistance as links lift progressively off the floor (a stepped, mass-based curve) rather than an elastic band’s continuously increasing tension; a mechanically different accommodating-resistance tool

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Chains draped over each bar end, deloading at the bottom and loading toward lockout.

candidates.name: Band-Resisted Squat

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Accommodating resistance on a loaded barbell squat; distinct from the seeded band-only "Band Squat".

candidates.name: Chain-Loaded Squat

candidates.notes: Chains draped over each end of the bar, deloading in the hole and loading near lockout.

candidates.name: Band-Resisted Deadlift

sources: Established S&C/powerlifting coaching literature (specialty-bar and accommodating-resistance texts: e.g. Westside Barbell conjugate-method material, EliteFTS/Elitefts specialty-bar guides)
candidates.notes: Accommodating resistance on a loaded barbell deadlift; distinct from the seeded band-only "Band Deadlift".

observations: Trap-bar deadlift: only one handle height is currently seeded ("Trap Bar Deadlift"); this agent could not confirm from the corpus alone whether that row is the high- or low-handle version, so treated it as the higher/shorter-pull default and added "Trap Bar Deadlift (Low Handle)" as the distinct longer-ROM variant per EL-2 range/depth class.
Nordic curl variants: already saturated (4 existing rows: Nordic Curl, Nordic Hamstring Curl, Nordic Glute Curl, Reverse Nordic Curl); no new Nordic row added.

Pallof variants: already saturated on cable (4 existing rows); no new cable Pallof row added. The landmine family’s "Landmine Anti-Rotation Press (Half-Kneeling)" covers the same anti-rotation intent on a different implement.

Glute-ham raise, reverse hyperextension, safety-bar squat, cambered-bar squat, Zercher squat, Jefferson squat, sissy squat (bodyweight and machine), Spanish squat, belt squat, GHD sit-up, plate pinch, wrist roller, hand gripper, neck harness: all already seeded; no new rows added for these, per EL-3 (would duplicate an existing stimulus).

Poliquin step-up and Peterson step-up: checked against the existing step-up rows. "Peterson Step-Up" (forward torso lean, glute-dominant execution) reads as the same stimulus as the seeded "Step-Up (Glute Focus)" and is recorded as an alias, not a new row. "Poliquin Step-Up" (controlled-eccentric, no push-off cue) is a coaching-technique variant on the same generic step-up pattern, not a different prime mover or loading vector under EL-2, so it is recorded as an alias of "Step-Up (Dumbbell)" rather than added as a row.
